clues.title: Sign: Town signs
text: Town entry signs in Bulgaria have a simple white design and use both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets. Like directional signs, the two lines of text are clear and visible even from a distance.

clues.title: Pole: Alternating pole top
text: This style of pole top, featuring 3 large, alternating insulators shaped like upward-facing hooks, is a good clue for Bulgaria. This pole top is likely unique to the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Small alternating hooks
text: Most poles in Bulgaria have small, alternating hook-shaped insulators, which can also be found in other countries (mostly on wooden poles, like Latvia, North Macedonia, and a few others). However, if you see them on a concrete pole, you're most likely in Bulgaria. Try using other clues to confirm.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: 4 Stripes + Hat Bulgaria
text: **Hat** - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > those with **4 Zebra Stripes**: Bulgaria.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Bulgaria usually has thin roadlines.
This is particularly useful to tell Bulgaria apart from Romania, where roadlines are usually much thicker.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 Winter
text: The majority of Generation 3 coverage in Bulgaria was taken during March and April, resulting in very distinct dead-looking “winter” coverage.
Hungary and Czechia also have a lot of similar dead-looking Generation 3 coverage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Grey Tape
text: You can commonly see a small piece of grey tape at the top of the car antenna in Generation 3 coverage.
Not all Gen 3 coverage has this tape.
This can also be seen in Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, and Romania.

clues.title: Chevron: Chevrons
text: Bulgarian chevrons are typically red on white.
Many other European countries have similar chevrons.
Crucially, among neighbouring countries, Romania, Turkey, and North Macedonia use the same chevrons.
Greece and Serbia use black and white chevrons however.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: Bollards are generally **fairly rare** in Bulgaria.

When you see them, they almost always have this somewhat generic design, which is relatively similar to the bollards found in Croatia and Hungary. They have a red reflector on the front, and a white one on the back. The design isn’t terribly consistent: sometimes they are thinner, and the shape of the reflector varies.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Patches Of Mortar
text: Most houses in Bulgaria have orange tiled roofs, with distinct patches of mortar along the corner tiles.
**Famously, Bulgarian roofs often seem poorly constructed:**
The roof tiles and mortar tend to be uneven, especially when compared to other European countries.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Ghetto-Like Look
text: Suburbs in Bulgaria are generally among the poorest areas in Europe, with small, densely built houses and generally an almost ghetto-like look.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: South - Alpine Architecture
text: Buildings with features similar to Alpine architecture, such as white walls with brown wooden details are commonly found in and around the Smoljan region in the south.

clues.title: Give way sign: Bulgaria
text: Conveniently, they are ordered by first digit, so just learning the first digit can yield high results with little effort.
Numbers between parentheses in the map are area codes from a neighbouring province that frequently spill into that one.
Codes next to a small dot represent area codes unique to the province capital.

clues.title: Language: Bulgarian
text: Bulgarian is a South Slavic language, closely related to Macedonian. Bulgarian mainly uses the Cyrillic alphabet, but many signs are written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts. The letter **Ъ** is only found in Bulgarian and Russian, although it is fairly uncommon in Russian, and is thus a good way to identify Bulgarian.
The Bulgarian word for street is **улица** (ulitsa), sometimes abbreviated **ул.** (ul.). This is the same as most Slavic languages (Russian, Serbian...).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
